source.title: Does a single direction mediate refusal? A small reproduction

record.file_problem: None; the full blog text is present.
record.tranche_reason: The post explicitly reproduces the difference-of-means direction procedure and tests ablation and addition on held-out prompts, with a norm-matched random-direction control.
record.gate_note: The real-model results are on Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct and Gemma 3 1B. The browser toy is explicitly synthetic, not a language model, so it is not included as a model result. Layer-selection values and results cited from other papers are not included.
record.test_reason: The post reproduces the difference-in-means refusal direction on Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct. It ablates the direction at all layers and adds it at layer 14 on held-out prompts, against norm-matched random controls. Follow-ups test whether a second suppression direction or over-refusal directions add anything beyond d1.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The author also concludes that over-refusal on this model is real and distinct from the harmful-refusal direction, but rides a single shared axis rather than per-category directions. The author treats the second-direction and over-refusal results as bounded negatives limited to this 1.5B model.
record.recipe_differences: The post says it uses the paper's difference-of-means construction and all-layer ablation, with addition at a selected layer. It uses a small-model reproduction, held-out splits, a norm-matched random control, and a coarse substring refusal classifier; only one tested model had enough baseline refusal for the main causal test.
record.method_sensitivity: Baseline refusal affected whether the procedure could be tested: Gemma 3 1B fell below the preset 0.5 floor. The tested over-refusal geometry changed with the estimator (raw versus whitened), though the whitened per-category cosine remained above the reveal band. The main direction was selected at layer 14; addition was tested there.
record.problems: The main positive result is on one 1.5B instruct model; Gemma 3 1B could not be tested because baseline refusal was below the preset floor. Refusal is measured with a coarse substring classifier. The post reports two seeds but no error bars or confidence intervals. General capability preservation was not measured.
record.rows_left_out: No own real-model outcome on the claim was omitted. Excluded layer-selection values used to choose the layer, the synthetic planted-direction toy, and results attributed to other papers.

untested.parts: Preservation of general capabilities was not measured. Addition was tested only at layer 14. Only one model (1.5B) was testable, since Gemma 3 1B failed the baseline floor.
Affine and cone accounts were not compared. Second directions came only from a cheap SOM/k-means proxy and FalseReject over-refusal fits on one model.
No separation of harmfulness judgment from the refusal decision.
No cross-language, cross-variant, or base-to-instruct transfer.

missing.what: Numeric safe-target refusal rates for the whitened addition arm: d1, d1+global, d1+per-category mean, d1+control
Second-seed rates for the global over-refusal addition arm (stated only as 'A second seed agreed')
missing.locator: What I do not think this shows, first over-refusal step

record.verdict_notes: The post is not an original source. The main V1 test rests on one model, scored with a substring classifier and without error bars. R15's d1-alone value (0.60) below the R14 unsteered rate (0.83) is unexplained in the text and may reflect different prompt subsets.

versions.untested_parts: General capability preservation was not measured. Addition was tested at the selected layer, not across all layers. Gemma 3 1B did not meet the preset baseline-refusal threshold, so its direction effect could not be tested.
No weight edit or released-model abliteration was tested.
No jailbreak attack or training against ablation was tested.
The follow-ups test a second suppression direction and over-refusal directions on one model; they do not directly compare affine, cone, and other general geometric accounts across models.
No separate harmfulness judgment and refusal-decision representation was measured.
No cross-language, base-to-instruct, or model-variant transfer test was conducted.
No comparison of refusal-training methods or training stages was conducted.

relation.reason: The post reports its own intervention results, with controls, on whether the direction mediates refusal and whether more directions add anything.

tranche.reason: Same method as the original: difference-of-means direction at the final instruction token, ablation at all layers, addition at the chosen layer, scored with the original's substring refusal classifier. Rates are on held-out prompts, with added norm-matched random controls. The V4 follow-ups use other methods, but the main result is a T1 reproduction.

source_check.notes: The pack listed no [lN] ids for its verdicts, so label_ids no_id_1 to no_id_3 follow pack order. The author is named in the text (Michael Leung). The date isn't stated; the post cites 2026 papers. The text says the model wrongly refuses 0.83 of the FalseReject prompts, yet +d1 safe-target refusal is 0.60. The unsteered rate for the addition arm isn't given, so the R16/R17 baselines are d1-only. The V4 follow-ups were run after the post was first published.

statements.correction: Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct, layer 14, harmful prompts. Single-layer d1 ablation: 1.00 to 0.50. With {d1,d2} (SOM/k-means proxy): 0.50. Random orthogonal control: 0.44. The second seed agreed; its numbers aren't stated.
statements.problem: The numbers for this study are right. One small point: the fitted second direction gave no raw gain at all (0.50 = 0.50), so for this study there was no gain that could 'vanish' against the null.

statements.correction: Over-refusal axis vs d1: cosine 0.49 raw, 0.26 whitened; the author calls it distinct. Safe-target refusal: +d1 0.60, +{d1,d_over} 0.81, +{d1,control} 0.56; this misses the pre-set add-margin past d1 alone. Per-category axes vs each other: mean |cos| 0.88 raw, 0.80 whitened (primary seed), 0.803 whitened (second seed), all above the 0.60 reveal band.
statements.problem: The numbers are right, but the study is filed under 'overlap with the main refusal direction'. The post calls the over-refusal axis distinct from d1, and whitening moves it further away (cosine 0.26). The near-parallel overlap is among the per-category over-refusal axes, not with d1. Also, 0.60 is the rate with d1 added, not the unsteered rate.

statements.correction: Single-layer d1 ablation at layer 14: 0.50. {d1,d2}: 0.50. Random orthogonal control: 0.44. The author calls it a bounded negative for a cheap second direction.
Random orthogonal control: 0.44. Fitted SOM/k-means-proxy second direction: 0.50. Both are with single-layer d1 ablation at layer 14 on harmful prompts.

At 1.5B this study found no gain from a cheap second direction: {d1,d2} 0.50, the same as d1 alone, against 0.44 for the random control. Over-refusal adds one distinct axis that misses its pre-set margin, not a family of axes.
statements.problem: The statement is cut off and no row is cited. The visible part says nothing about this study. If it were cited as support for 'several directions remove more refusal than one at 1-10B', that would be wrong.
